claims.assertion: This was an instant RydeX booking (not RydeTAXI) accepted at 17:12:00 and cancelled by the rider at 17:15:05, so the NS-0 rider-cancellation branch routes the $6.61 fee to NS-4.

At the moment of cancellation the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2185 m and the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius, so the driver was not at Bedok Mall and could not have been waiting there.

The platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1 conditions (i) and (ii) both fail.

The driver his own written admission that he was still "on my way" when the rider cancelled, confirming no arrival and no wait at the pickup point; even his chat message promised about 5 minutes, i.e. arrival after 17:18, which the 17:15:05 cancellation preceded.

The driver's account must not be treated as a valid no-show claim: his excuse was traffic, yet the only traffic record is a band-3 (20-29 km/h) speed band on Sim Avenue East and no traffic incident was recorded, and the weather was fair, so nothing justifies his absence from the pickup point.

Because NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full to the rider; the fee on record is exactly $6.61 with no surge applied, so the refund amount is $6.61.

The driver has 2 disputes with 2 upheld no-show findings in the last 90 days, and the complaint was filed within the 30-day window, supporting the refund (in voucher form per NS-7) and an account-review flag on the driver for repeated unmet pickups.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 minutes 5 seconds after matching (F2), which is just past the 3:00 mark, so on its face the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4) makes the $6.61 fee chargeable and the rider needs NS-2's failure of the driver-side conditions to succeed.

Ryde has no published rule allowing a free cancellation when the driver is late versus ETA (NS-8 is informational only, and the case file has no ETA field); the driver's chat line "About 5 min, traffic" (F8) is a promise of arrival time, not proof of a binding deadline, so the judge may treat the 17:15:05 cancellation as premature.

The rider's own chat asked only "How long will you be?" (F7) and never said she was cancelling; the delay argument rests mainly on the driver's absence from the pickup point rather than on any agreed cutoff.

The driver's statement (F10) does not by itself prove a no-show failure, and the traffic band record (F11) shows some congestion on one road, which the driver may cite to explain his distance from the pickup point.

events.body:
D1: The rider, not the driver, cancelled this trip: the timeline records cancellation_by rider at 17:15:05 (F2), so the $6.61 fee can only arise under NS-0's rider-cancellation branch, i.e. NS-4 for an on-demand RydeX booking (F2, F5). [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
D2: NS-4 turns solely on elapsed time since matching: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05) and 5 seconds is beyond the 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is validly charged and the correct outcome on this branch is no_action (F2, F5). [F2 F5] [NS-4 NS-0]
D3: The rider's stated ground — 'the driver was still far away' — is not a ground for a free cancellation in the policy: NS-4 provides no waiver for a driver who has not yet reached the pickup point, and the policy discloses no ETA-based free-cancellation rule, so the rider's remedy is a human appeal under NS-7, not a refund on the merits (F1, F2, F8). [F1 F2 F8] [NS-4]
D4: The only basis in the case record on which this fee could fall away — the rider-cancellation branch of NS-4 — is not displaced by NS-1/NS-2, because those clauses govern the situation where the driver cancels for a rider no-show; here the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and never cancelled (F2, F3, F4). [F2 F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2 NS-0]
D5: The driver's conduct before cancellation was communicative and consistent with the trip being live: at 17:12 the rider asked 'How long will you be?' and at 17:13 the driver answered 'About 5 min, traffic' — notice given roughly 2 minutes before the cancellation, leaving the rider the choice to wait or cancel with knowledge of the position (F7, F8, F2). [F7 F8 F2] [NS-4]
D6: The driver's 'traffic' explanation matches the only traffic record in the case window: SIMS AVENUE EAST was recorded in speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) from 17:07 to 17:20, i.e. congested but moving, and no incident was recorded near the route (F8, F11, F12; weather fair, F13) — this explains slow progress, not a refusal to serve. [F8 F11 F12 F13] [NS-4]
D7: The chat record is complete — 2 messages, all timestamped (F9) — so no fact of this case falls into the missing-evidence category that would force escalation; there is nothing left undetermined to excuse the fee (F9, F2, F4). [F9] [NS-7]
Weaknesses: F1 is the rider's strongest fact: the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 2185 m at 17:15:05 and he never entered 200 m, so on NS-4's wording the fee stands only because the policy contains no ETA-based waiver — a judge sympathetic to the rider may treat the fee as unfair even though the policy compels no_action. | F3 and F4 record driver_arrived_at = null and driver_pressed_here_at = null; although these are neutral on the rider-cancellation branch, they deprive me of any NS-1/NS-2 argument and confirm the driver never reached the pickup point. | F8 ('About 5 min, traffic') written at 17:13 is arguably consistent with the rider's complaint and sits next to a 3 min 5 s cancellation — the other side can read it as an admission that the promised arrival was well after the fee window; it also tends to shift the DBQ toward the rider's account, and my 'traffic' mitigation rests only on one band-3 road reading (F11) with no incident evidence (F12). | F15 is against my client on the whole: 2 disputes and 2 upheld (no-show: 2) in 90 days, so any request for leniency on the rider's behalf by the driver is undermined by the profile record, and the rider's own clean profile (F14: 4.1 y, 0 disputes) makes their grievance look more credible.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
Safety screen first: the only chat is the rider asking "How long will you be?" [F7] and the driver replying "About 5 min, traffic" [F8]; the driver's post-trip statement [F10] is "I was on my way when the rider cancelled", and the complaint is confined to the fee. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not engaged [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

On the merits this is a rider cancellation of an instant RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the $6.61 fee to the rider-cancellation branch, i.e. NS-4 [F2][F5][NS-0][NS-4]. The trace settles the two NS-4 elements: the rider (not the driver) cancelled [F2], and cancellation came 185 s (3 min 5 s) after acceptance at 17:12:00 — 5 seconds past the 3:00 grace window [F2][NS-4]. NS-4 therefore charges the fee and the outcome is no_action [F5][NS-4].

The rider's route to a refund is NS-2, but NS-2 only operates within the driver-cancellation branch of NS-0 (driver cancels on a no-show claim and NS-1(i)-(iii) fail) [NS-0][NS-1][NS-2]. Here the driver never cancelled and, consistently, never tapped "I'm Here" and has no recorded arrival [F3][F4]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This was an instant RydeX booking (not RydeTAXI) accepted at 17:12:00 and cancelled by the rider at 17:15:05, so the NS-0 rider-cancellation branch routes the $6.61 fee to NS-4.

At the moment of cancellation the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2185 m and the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius, so the driver was not at Bedok Mall and could not have been waiting there.

The platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1 conditions (i) and (ii) both fail.

The driver his own written admission that he was still "on my way" when the rider cancelled, confirming no arrival and no wait at the pickup point; even his chat message promised about 5 minutes, i.e. arrival after 17:18, which the 17:15:05 cancellation preceded.

The driver's account must not be treated as a valid no-show claim: his excuse was traffic, yet the only traffic record is a band-3 (20-29 km/h) speed band on Sim Avenue East and no traffic incident was recorded, and the weather was fair, so nothing justifies his absence from the pickup point.

Because NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full to the rider; the fee on record is exactly $6.61 with no surge applied, so the refund amount is $6.61.

The driver has 2 disputes with 2 upheld no-show findings in the last 90 days, and the complaint was filed within the 30-day window, supporting the refund (in voucher form per NS-7) and an account-review flag on the driver for repeated unmet pickups.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 minutes 5 seconds after matching (F2), which is just past the 3:00 mark, so on its face the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4) makes the $6.61 fee chargeable and the rider needs NS-2's failure of the driver-side conditions to succeed.

Ryde has no published rule allowing a free cancellation when the driver is late versus ETA (NS-8 is informational only, and the case file has no ETA field); the driver's chat line "About 5 min, traffic" (F8) is a promise of arrival time, not proof of a binding deadline, so the judge may treat the 17:15:05 cancellation as premature.

The rider's own chat asked only "How long will you be?" (F7) and never said she was cancelling; the delay argument rests mainly on the driver's absence from the pickup point rather than on any agreed cutoff.

The driver's statement (F10) does not by itself prove a no-show failure, and the traffic band record (F11) shows some congestion on one road, which the driver may cite to explain his distance from the pickup point.

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled this trip: the timeline records cancellation_by rider at 17:15:05 (F2), so the $6.61 fee can only arise under NS-0's rider-cancellation branch, i.e. NS-4 for an on-demand RydeX booking (F2, F5).

NS-4 turns solely on elapsed time since matching: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05) and 5 seconds is beyond the 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is validly charged and the correct outcome on this branch is no_action (F2, F5).

The rider's stated ground — 'the driver was still far away' — is not a ground for a free cancellation in the policy: NS-4 provides no waiver for a driver who has not yet reached the pickup point, and the policy discloses no ETA-based free-cancellation rule, so the rider's remedy is a human appeal under NS-7, not a refund on the merits (F1, F2, F8).

The only basis in the case record on which this fee could fall away — the rider-cancellation branch of NS-4 — is not displaced by NS-1/NS-2, because those clauses govern the situation where the driver cancels for a rider no-show; here the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and never cancelled (F2, F3, F4).

The driver's conduct before cancellation was communicative and consistent with the trip being live: at 17:12 the rider asked 'How long will you be?' and at 17:13 the driver answered 'About 5 min, traffic' — notice given roughly 2 minutes before the cancellation, leaving the rider the choice to wait or cancel with knowledge of the position (F7, F8, F2).

The driver's 'traffic' explanation matches the only traffic record in the case window: SIMS AVENUE EAST was recorded in speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) from 17:07 to 17:20, i.e. congested but moving, and no incident was recorded near the route (F8, F11, F12; weather fair, F13) — this explains slow progress, not a refusal to serve.

The chat record is complete — 2 messages, all timestamped (F9) — so no fact of this case falls into the missing-evidence category that would force escalation; there is nothing left undetermined to excuse the fee (F9, F2, F4).

weaknesses: F1 is the rider's strongest fact: the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 2185 m at 17:15:05 and he never entered 200 m, so on NS-4's wording the fee stands only because the policy contains no ETA-based waiver — a judge sympathetic to the rider may treat the fee as unfair even though the policy compels no_action.

F3 and F4 record driver_arrived_at = null and driver_pressed_here_at = null; although these are neutral on the rider-cancellation branch, they deprive me of any NS-1/NS-2 argument and confirm the driver never reached the pickup point.

F8 ('About 5 min, traffic') written at 17:13 is arguably consistent with the rider's complaint and sits next to a 3 min 5 s cancellation — the other side can read it as an admission that the promised arrival was well after the fee window; it also tends to shift the DBQ toward the rider's account, and my 'traffic' mitigation rests only on one band-3 road reading (F11) with no incident evidence (F12).

F15 is against my client on the whole: 2 disputes and 2 upheld (no-show: 2) in 90 days, so any request for leniency on the rider's behalf by the driver is undermined by the profile record, and the rider's own clean profile (F14: 4.1 y, 0 disputes) makes their grievance look more credible.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: the rider did cancel, so NS-0 sends the fee through the rider branch — but NS-0's rider branch is not free-standing, it must still be measured against the driver's own compliance record (F2, F4), and my case is that the fee fails on its own facts rather than on a competing branch.

The 5-second overrun only fixes the fee under NS-4 if the trip was a genuine live trip; where driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null (F3, F4) and the closest approach was 2185 m at the very second of cancellation (F1), the fee cannot stand as a charge for a service that was never tendered, and NS-2's refund_full is the applicable remedy.

NS-4 assumes the driver was performing the trip; here the GPS record shows the driver 2185 m away at 17:15:05 and never within 200 m (F1, F3), so the fee is not a valid no-show charge at all and the rider's remedy is the NS-2 refund, not merely an NS-7 appeal.

NS-1/NS-2 are not confined to a driver-initiated cancellation: NS-0 routes driver no-show claims through NS-1/NS-2, and here the no-show claim collapses because the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' (F4) and never reached the pickup (F1, F3) — the exact NS-2 refund conditions.

The driver's own 17:13 message promised "About 5 min, traffic" (F8), i.e. arrival around 17:18, and his written statement admits he was still "on my way" when the rider cancelled (F10) — the notice he gave was notice that he would not reach Bedok Mall inside the fee window, not notice of a tendered pickup.

The traffic record undercuts rather than supports the driver: SIMS AVENUE EAST at band 3 (20-29 km/h) is moving traffic and the only band level recorded, no incident was logged near the route (F12), and weather was fair (F13) — none of this explains a driver still 2185 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation (F1).

A complete chat record (F9) does not create a valid fee; it simply means no G12 escalation is needed, and on these facts the record proves the driver was en route, not at the pickup (F8, F10), so the fee must be refunded under NS-2.

I withdraw nothing but refine C4's reading: the driver's "About 5 min, traffic" message (F8) and his post-trip statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" (F10) together show a driver who had not arrived, which is exactly why the fee fails — not merely a promise-breaking point.
The refund figure stays $6.61 because that is the exact fee on record with no surge applied (F5, F6), and NS-7 permits it to be issued as a voucher.

Conceded as to the framework: the rider cancelled an instant RydeX booking 3 min 5 s after matching (F2), so NS-0 sends the fee to NS-4 - and NS-4 charges it, since 17:15:05 is 5 seconds past the 3:00 grace window.

This fact is not in dispute and does not help the rider: F1 (2185 m, never within 200 m at 17:15:05; F1 also carries no off-route or extra-km entry via the route facts) addresses conditions NS-1(i)-(ii), which only apply where the DRIVER cancels for a no-show - the driver did not cancel here, so NS-1/NS-2 never engage (F2).

Agreed on the values (F3 driver_arrived_at null, F4 driver_pressed_here_at null), but a null arrival record only means no NS-1 no-show fee was earned - it does not generate any refund obligation, because the fee on the record was levied on the rider-cancellation branch (F2, F5).

F10 ('I was on my way when the rider cancelled') is consistent with the system record, not adverse: the driver had accepted at 17:12:00 and was en route when the rider pulled the trip at 17:15:05 (F2), and F8's 'About 5 min' is an estimate given at 17:13, not an admitted breach of any policy deadline (NS-4 sets no ETA deadline).

This misplaces the burden: the driver never made a no-show claim, so nothing needs to be 'justified' (F2, F4); and F11's band 3 (20-29 km/h) on Sims Avenue East during 17:07-17:20 corroborates the driver's 17:13 'traffic' line (F8), with F12/F13 merely showing there was no incident or rain, not that the roads were clear.

NS-2 does not apply: it refunds the fee only where the DRIVER cancels for a rider no-show and NS-1 (i)-(iii) fail, and here the rider cancelled (F2), so the governing clause is NS-4, which charges the fee because 17:15:05 is past the 3-minute mark (F2, F5, F6).

F15 supports, at most, an account-review flag - policy forbids using profile facts to decide the case itself - and here no driver-side violation is established, so RD-6 cannot attach; the correct outcome on the merits is no_action on the $6.61.
